items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was an innovator. He was one in the forefront of whatever. He had his place. I appreciated it.

ctx.x: As soon as you say Faubus -­

Yeah, I know, Fables of Faubus. There’s just some people out there that I’m not concerned with getting as far into it as they were, Miles and Mingus and Monk. They had their special place that nobody can invade. As I said before, there’s too much love in my music and too much joy and happiness. I love the idea of playing happy music, happy jazz, happy swinging jazz. That’s what Basie was all about. That music was happy. That’s why people were enjoying it so much. One reason, it swung, it was happy. It made them…
Can I just ask another question? Kenny Clarke, you played with Kenny Clarke. You played with Boo, Art Blakey. You played with Elvin. But what was playing with Kenny Clarke like?
